text:
alex: FYI saw a hard OOM on prod-rt-3 during a long customer session (~95k tokens). Looks correlated with KV rotation spikes + kernel switch. Reproting here to coordinate a short mitigation.
ops-bot: [ALERT] instance prod-rt-3 OOM at 2025-07-08T14:12:03Z. Group: eng-runtime. Incident id: i-7f2c.
priya: Can you paste the allocator trace and the runtime kernel selection log?
alex: quick paste — allocator shows repeated large KV slab allocs then immediate fail:
```
oom: failed to allocate 1.1GiB slab for kv_page
kv_rotate: candidate size=1.2GiB, shard=7
kernel_switch: selected kernel="opt-attn-v2" prior="opt-attn-v1"
trace: kv_alloc@serve.cc:312 -> page_manager::reserve() -> oom
```
marco: Interesting — kernel v2 has ~8% more meta structure for per-token state; with rotation it pushes slab footprints up. Batching heuristics also spiked the sequence length distribution at that moment.
jamie: Did we see concurrent large prefix cache misses? paging count went up?
alex: yes, pageouts jumped from ~30/s to ~220/s for that pod in the 20s leading up to crash. Pattern: long ongoing convo + model switched to kernel v2 mid-request due to a latency heuristic.
taylor: Could be race between batcher choosing faster kernel for shorter latencies while kv rotation (background compaction) was underway — double whammy.
marco: Repro plan: run a 100k token session with forced kernel-v2 switch at 70k, enable background compaction. That should exercise both.
priya: For immediate mitigation on prod: recommend (1) pin kernel to v1 for pods serving >50k token sessions, (2) raise soft_evict threshold from 0.75 -> 0.85, (3) add a KV-rotation throttle that prevents rotation when live_alloc > 0.6*capacity.
alex: I pushed a canary: pinned kernel to v1 for 2 pods in prod-rt-3, increased soft_evict. Will monitor.
deploy-bot: deploy start: rollback window 15m. change: runtime config kv.soft_evict=0.85, kernel.pin=opt-attn-v1 on prod-rt-3-*.
ops-bot: deploy succeeded on 2/2 canary pods.
jamie: Also a short-term graceful degrade: if kv allocation fails, runtime should surface a soft-fallback that disables prefix caching for that session and continues in stateless incremental mode rather than OOMing. We have a codepath for that but it wasn't triggered because the allocator aborts early.
marco: Right — allocator aborts on hard OOM. We need an intermediate path: try reserve_with_backoff(max_retries=3, prefer_spill=true) then if still fail, call kv_disable_prefix_cache_for_session(session_id).
priya: Telemetry change request: emit a metric kv.reserve.backoff.count and kv.rotation.throttle.active with tags {pod, kernel_selected, live_alloc_ratio}.
taylor: Also verify batching heuristic: the decision function was using p95 latency windows that moment — maybe need to include live_alloc_ratio as an input to avoid switching kernels when memory headroom is low.
alex: After canary changes, memory headroom stabilized. No further OOMs in the last 20m. I'll leave the pins for 1h then try a staged rollback to let kernel switch but with rotation throttle.
jamie: Action items:
- marco: add reserve_with_backoff + spill fallback (PR) — priority P0, estimate 1d.
- priya: add metrics and dashboard tile for live_alloc_ratio + rotation throttle — estimate 4h.
- taylor: update kernel selection feature flag to include memory headroom signal — estimate 6h.
- alex: monitor and coordinate rollback plan in 1h.
marco: Noted. I'll start the PR and add unit tests for reserve_backoff behavior.
priya: I'll update the oncall runbook with the KV-rotation throttle and immediate mitigation steps (pin kernel, raise soft_evict).
alex: thanks everyone. If anybody sees related OOM traces, drop them here. :thumbsup:
